verdict.rationale: Microsoft Graph's first-party docs describe an upload session that lets an app upload ranges of a file in sequential requests and resume the transfer if the connection drops. That is exactly the chunked, resumable mechanism the story asks for. The single-call PUT is documented as capped at 250 MB, which positions upload sessions as the path for big files. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of resume reliability, documented detail on fragment size limits and session expiry/resume-status mechanics.

support.subject: As a developer, big files upload reliably — documented chunked/resumable upload sessions that survive a dropped connection

citations.quote: An upload session allows your app to upload ranges of the file in sequential API requests. It also enables the transfer to resume if the connection is dropped during the upload.
This method only supports files up to 250 MB in size.
